summary: This short wiki entry describes Sidney Peel, a member of the Peel family. It places him as the second son of Arthur Peel, 1st Viscount Peel, and gives his mother as Adelaide, daughter of William Stratford Dugdale. It also records his service as Member of Parliament for Uxbridge from 1918 to 1922, his rank of Colonel in the British Army, and his 1936 creation as a Baronet.
one_line: Sidney Peel, son of Viscount Peel and grandson of Prime Minister Robert Peel, was an MP for Uxbridge, British Army colonel, and 1936 baronet.
key_facts: Sidney Peel was the second son of Arthur Peel, 1st Viscount Peel, who was Speaker of the House of Commons.
The note describes Arthur Peel, 1st Viscount Peel, as the youngest son of Prime Minister Sir Robert Peel, Bt.
Sidney Peel's mother was Adelaide, daughter of William Stratford Dugdale.
Sidney Peel sat as Member of Parliament for Uxbridge between 1918 and 1922.
Sidney Peel was a Colonel in the British Army.
In 1936 Sidney Peel was created a Baronet, of Eyeworth in the County of Bedford.
